lesson.title: Find an L-shape's area
lesson.subtitle: P4 measurement revision
lesson.objective: Find an L-shape's area by two valid methods.
lesson.story: An outer 12 cm by 8 cm rectangle has a 4 cm by 3 cm corner removed.

steps.title: Choose a valid area method
steps.prompt: Choose one valid method to find the L-shape's area.

choices.label: Find the outer rectangle, then take away the removed corner.
Split into two rectangles that do not overlap, then add them.
Find the outer rectangle, then add on the removed corner too.

hints: The missing corner does not cover the L-shape.
You may subtract it from the outer rectangle.
You may also split the L-shape into two rectangles.
Both subtracting the corner and adding two non-overlapping parts work.

steps.title: Find the removed corner
steps.prompt: What is the area of the 4 cm by 3 cm corner? Answer in cm².
hints: Area of a rectangle is width × height.

steps.title: Find the L-shape's area
steps.prompt: An outer 12 cm by 8 cm rectangle has a 4 cm by 3 cm corner removed. Find its area in cm².
hints: Outer area is 96 cm²; removed area is 12 cm².

steps.title: Explain the measure

choices.label: An inside split line also counts as part of the perimeter.
Area counts square units; perimeter is only the outside edge.
Area and perimeter are both measured in the same units.

hints: Look at what is being measured.
Area covers a surface; perimeter goes around its boundary.
An inside teaching split is not an outside edge.
Choose the explanation that separates square units from boundary length.
